sentences.text:
2. Heard the learned counsel for the appellants and the learned SPP-II for respondent no.1/State and the learned counsel appearing for respondent no.2 is defacto complainant.
3.
The respondent no.2 has filed statement of objections.
4. On going through the entire complaint/First Information Report (for short 'FIR'), it is seen that the main allegations are against accused no.1, whose name is also shown in the FIR.

The allegations against the appellants are that appellant no.1 has provided Hyundai Venue Car bearing Reg.No.GJ 25 AA-2772 and also his Mobile phone to accused no.1 in order to facilitate him to escape from the clutches of the police and appellant no.2 being the driver of accused no.1, a resident of Kadakola,
Mysuru , inspite of knowing the criminal background and the history of accused no.1 helped him to travel in the said car from one State to another in order to facilitate him to escape from the police.
5. It is contended by the learned SPP-II that after registration of the case, accused no.1 has absconded and he went to Pune and from there he went to Gujarath.

On receiving a credible information about his whereabouts, he was apprehended from Ahmadabad along with the present appellants and therefore contends at this stage the involvement of the appellants is writ large.
6. According to the prosecution, accused no.3 is said to be the driver of accused no.1.
It is alleged that both the appellants have facilitated accused no.1 to abscond and they accompanied him throughout the journey and thus harbored him.
The offence alleged against them is under Section 212 of IPC.

Whether these appellants with the knowledge of the criminal background and registration of a case against the main accused have facilitated him to escape from the clutches of the police and provided him a car and also joined him throughout the journey and helped him to abscond in due course, is a matter to be established by the prosecution during trial.
As already observed the main allegations are against accused no.1.
Apart from the above allegations against the appellants herein, there are no other allegations.

7. The learned Sessions Judge while rejecting the prayer has observed that the involvement of these petitioners as alleged are to be investigated and further, investigation is under progress and therefore if the appellants are released then there is every chance that they may abscond from the jurisdiction of the court.
8. The learned counsel for the appellants submits that the appellants are ready to furnish sufficient surety to ensure their presence before the Trial Court.
He submits that the investigation is already completed and charge- sheet is also filed.
9. In the above facts and circumstances, the appellants who are already arrested, interrogated can be enlarged on bail by imposing suitable conditions.
Hence the following order.
ORDER The appeal is allowed.

They shall execute a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) with two solvent sureties out of which one surety shall be a local surety, to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.
